2.text: trembled. ‘Oh!’ she said to herself, ‘they will kill her.’ — ‘Let us go and look at that snow!’

3.text: They approached the snow. In the mean time the warm wind had caused the snow to thaw. Deep

4.text: holes are seen in the snow-drift. ‘What holes are these?’ says one. He thrusts his spear through

5.text: the snow, — one, two, three times, — almost wounding the girl. She is there, but wriggles like

6.text: a fish, and escapes being wounded. He thrusts again; then at last he wounds her upon the but-

7.text: tocks. She bites her lip and almost burrows into the ground, like a wounded female fox. Her

8.text: companion sits near by and weeps noiselessly. ‘Ah, ah! why are you weeping?’ — ‘I do not

9.text: know.’ — ‘Nay, she must be near by. Why is this one weeping?’ — ‘You lie,’ the girl says,

10.text: ‘unless you have put her there yourself. With what could we have made a hole like this in the

11.text: snow? With our nails? Have you seen any knives in our hands?’ — ‘Then why are you weeping
11.note: line ends bare 'weeping' with no trailing punctuation, verified at 2x; not fabricating a comma.

12.text: thus?’ — ‘Nay, I feel much sorrow in going to your people. Therefore I am weeping. To be

13.text: among you, a speechless stranger, is very hard for me. I see the men of your people for the first

14.text: time only. And also yesterday I could hardly walk for fatigue, but you drove me on. At the

15.text: memory of that I am weeping. And, furthermore; I hoped at least to be with my sister, and to

16.text: look on the face of my companion. Now I am quite alone. At the thought of that I am weeping.’
16.note: a small speck sits before 'face' in the raster; no letter is missing there, ruled a print artifact and not keyed.

17.text: The other girl was listening from her place of refuge. The men spoke among themselves. ‘It is

18.text: perhaps true. She is not here. We have thrust our spears through all this snow. Probably she

19.text: has fled home. Let us go! It is useless to stay here any longer.’ They went away and left the

20.text: fugitive. The other one says, ‘Now I will not walk in front, I will walk comfortably behind you.’

21.text: “When the sun was setting, the one concealed could not wait any longer. She said, ‘They

22.text: have probably gone.’ She crept out of the snow and went home. Two nights she had slept in

23.text: the open, lame and broken, all covered with blood. When she reached home, the youngest of the

24.text: brothers was not there. He was running about in the neighborhood, looking for the girls. The

25.text: other brothers began to kiss her. Where is your sister?’ She says nothing, nor does she show
25.note: the closing single quote after 'sister?' has no matching opening quote before 'Where' — the compositor's omission, keyed as printed per §2.14.

26.text: her wound. The youngest brother came home. He caught her in his arms, hugged her many

27.text: times, and could not have enough. ‘Where is your companion?’ Then she told him, ‘They have

28.text: ravished her.’ The older sister, on parting, told the younger one, ‘He who loves me most of all

29.text: will follow me.’ The youngest brother cannot sleep. ‘Where is my other sister?’ The wounded

30.text: girl says to herself, ‘About the wound I will tell him to-morrow. I do not want to deprive him
30.note: a small raised mark sits before 'deprive' in the raster; ruled a print artifact (bleed-through/speck), not a real apostrophe, and not keyed.

31.text: of his quiet just now. Let him have some sleep just this one night.’

32.text: “The youngest brother is strong and swift of foot. In the morning she said to him, ‘I am

33.text: ashamed to tell it, but I cannot walk.’ — ‘Why are you ashamed? Have I given you any

34.text: reason to be afraid of me? Or do you say to yourself, “If I tell him, he will not listen to me”?

35.text: Why are you ashamed?’ Then she showed him the wound, the hole in her clothes. ‘See that!’

36.text: says the girl. The young man gasped. ‘Oh! why have they wounded a woman? If they had

37.text: wounded a man, it would be easier to bear. It is shameful to wound women.’ Then he says to

38.text: his companions, ‘Now let us go and follow their road.’ The others said, ‘Not yet. We are not

39.text: ready!’ — ‘Oh! let us go! I cannot wait. It is too bad. Since seeing my sister’s wound, I

40.text: cannot stay here. I am a man. Then let me go.’ The others said, ‘We will sleep here this one

41.text: night.’ The youngest brother cannot sleep. He walks to and fro. Early in the morning he says

42.text: to his brothers, ‘Come, let us make haste. I call you to a war with the alien people. Great

43.text: anger came into my heart. With your help I shall be strong.’”

44.text: Then follows a description of a raid of the five brothers on the camp of

45.text: the ravishers. They kill every one, take the herd and their sister, and return

46.note: footnote marker: superscript 1 (U+00B9), matching the opener on line 52 ('¹ Bogoras, Chukchee Materials, p. 339.'); mz text had it as a stray ']'.

47.text: As mentioned before, this tale describes the ravishing of Chukchee girls

48.text: by men of an alien tribe. Besides this, according to the tradition, the ravish-

49.text: ing of women was practised also within the Chukchee tribe, and not longer

50.text: ago than forty or fifty years. There exists a special term for the ravishing

51.text: of women, ñaung̣ɪnteweˊerkɪn (“thou ravishest a woman”).
